text: if you are naming joints and you also need to declare the rotation for forward like a car, do you look at it head on, and then say left when if the camera is trailing that actually is the right or i assume probably not after typing that out but idk lol
resolution: User asked the joint-naming/orientation convention question (do you name left/right head-on or from a trailing camera, and how to declare forward rotation). Answered the convention (name from the vehicle's own/driver frame, which equals a trailing chase cam; head-on is the only view that mirrors left/right; the mirror plane separates left from right; the wheel spin axis is the lateral axle, set automatically). While explaining, fixed a real correctness nit it surfaced: the ⌖ wheel center button hardcoded the joint spin axis to [0,0,1] (Z), which is only right when the car's axle happens to be Z — changed it to use fit.axis (the fitted well's normal = the actual axle) so the declared spin axis is correct for any model orientation. Full hmsc-int cart bundles clean. Committed b3bef7ec8.
